[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Dimensionality Reduction in Machine Learning: PCA, t-SNE, and UMAP"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"High-dimensional data is a common challenge in machine learning. As the number of features increases, models often suffer from the curse of dimensionality, leading to overfitting and high computational costs. Dimensionality reduction techniques mitigate this by mapping high-dimensional data into a lower-dimensional space while preserving essential structural information."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Principal Component Analysis (PCA)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"PCA is a linear dimensionality reduction technique that identifies orthogonal axes, called principal components, which maximize the variance of the projected data. It is highly efficient and widely used for data compression and noise reduction."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
import numpy as np

# Generate dummy high-dimensional data
X = np.random.rand(100, 50)

# Initialize PCA to reduce to 2 dimensions
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X)

print("PCA shape:", X_pca.shape)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"t-SNE is a non-linear technique particularly well-suited for embedding high-dimensional data into a low-dimensional space of two or three dimensions for visualization. It converts Euclidean distances between data points into conditional probabilities that represent similarities, minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence between distributions."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.manifold import TSNE

# Initialize t-SNE
tsne = TSNE(n_components=2, perplexity=30.0, random_state=42)
X_tsne = tsne.fit_transform(X)

print("t-SNE shape:", X_tsne.shape)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"UMAP is a non-linear manifold learning technique based on Riemannian geometry and algebraic topology. Compared to t-SNE, UMAP often preserves more of the global data structure while maintaining fast computation times and scalability for large datasets."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"import umap

# Initialize UMAP
reducer = umap.UMAP(n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1, random_state=42)
X_umap = reducer.fit_transform(X)

print("UMAP shape:", X_umap.shape)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Comparison and Best Practices"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"PCA: Linear, highly scalable, excellent for feature extraction, noise reduction, and preprocessing before supervised training."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"t-SNE: Non-linear, excels at visualizing local clusters, but computationally expensive and struggles with preserving global structures."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"UMAP: Non-linear, faster than t-SNE, preserves both local and global structure effectively, and scales well to large datasets."}]
